title: A polar arch: area, distance from the y-axis, motion toward the origin and a tangent slope

stimulus.title: The curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>
stimulus.html: The curve shown is the graph of the polar equation r=3sin⁡θ+cos⁡(2θ)r = 3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta) for 0≤θ≤π0 \le \theta \le \pi. It starts at the point (1,0)(1, 0) and ends at (−1,0)(-1, 0). Region RR is bounded by the curve and the xx-axis. A graphing calculator is required, in radian mode.

parts.label: a

rubric.point: Integrand: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\left(3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta)\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math>, with both the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and the square

accept: an equivalent split of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math> into pieces

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Area</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Area}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi} \left(3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta)\right)^2 d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5.854</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5.854</annotation></semantics></math> (calculator).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For 0≤θ≤π20 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}, find the greatest distance from a point on the curve to the yy-axis. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: Distance from the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= r\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta)\right)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, considered on the interval
accept: solving <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(\theta) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = r\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Answer <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.737</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.737</annotation></semantics></math>, justified by comparing the critical point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.480</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta \approx 0.480</annotation></semantics></math> with the endpoints (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.737</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.737</annotation></semantics></math> from the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \frac{\pi}{2}]</annotation></semantics></math> with the endpoint values

parts.sample: The distance from the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= r(\theta)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta)\right)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, which is not negative on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \frac{\pi}{2}]</annotation></semantics></math>. On the calculator, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(\theta) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.480</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0.480</annotation></semantics></math> (store it as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>). Candidates: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1.737</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(A) = 1.737</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. The greatest distance is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.737</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.737</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Is the point on the curve moving toward the origin or away from the origin as θ\theta increases through θ=5π6\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Values: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = 2 > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><msub><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}\Big|_{\theta = 5\pi/6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.866</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -0.866 < 0</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r' = 3\cos\theta - 2\sin(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated
the signs of both, with values

rubric.point: Conclusion with reason: toward the origin, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing (opposite signs of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: the distance from the origin is decreasing

not earned with the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> alone, without <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r > 0</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3\cos\theta - 2\sin(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><msub><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}\Big|_{\theta = 5\pi/6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.866</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -0.866 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is positive and decreasing, the distance from the origin is decreasing: the point is moving toward the origin.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line tangent to the curve at the point where θ=π3\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}.

rubric.point: Setup: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = r\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = r\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{r'\sin\theta + r\cos\theta}{r'\cos\theta - r\sin\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>

calculator derivatives of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\theta)\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\theta)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Answer <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.439</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.439</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.438</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.438</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: not earned by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.232</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.232</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = r\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = r\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3\sin\theta + \cos(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> the calculator gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.848</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta} = 0.848</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.933</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -1.933</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.439</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -0.439</annotation></semantics></math>.
